---
title: From pipelines to prompts
subtitle: NLP in the LLM era
author: Marie-Hélène Burle
---

:::{.def}

Traditional [natural language processing (NLP)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing) relied on task-specific pipelines (for sentiment analysis, entities recognition, topic modelling, etc.) and labour-intensive labeled datasets. Today, a single pre-trained [large language model (LLM)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model) can handle all tasks through plain-language prompts.

But is a generative model always the right tool for the job?

In this webinar, I will compare the results, data constraints, and compute requirements of running the same tasks on the same corpus through three eras of NLP: the classic pipeline, text embeddings, and prompting a small LLM. We will see that embeddings remain a practical and efficient choice for semantic search and classification, especially on smaller datasets.

:::

*Coming up on October 27.*
